title: How AI Agents Pay: Checkout in ChatGPT and Google AI Mode — Sam Parsons, PayPal
talk_summary: A PayPal engineer demos three ways merchants can accept agent-initiated payments: ChatGPT instant checkout via an MCP app plus the agentic commerce protocol, Google AI Mode via the universal commerce protocol, and a generic MCP-app-plus-external-checkout handoff. The core mechanism is tokenization: the host exchanges a real payment credential for a scoped token (merchant-bound, max amount, currency, expiry) that the merchant then charges.

takeaways.technique: Scoped capability tokens instead of raw credentials
takeaways.what_they_do: The host tokenizes the user's payment credential and passes the merchant a token constrained to one merchant, a max amount, a currency, and an expiration, so the sensitive credential never travels through the agent chain.

takeaways.technique: MCP app with embedded UI plus external-checkout handoff and session callback
takeaways.what_they_do: The merchant ships an MCP app whose widget renders product UI inside the host agent, then hands off to an external checkout page tied by a session, and the widget auto-updates when the external flow completes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when they click checkout this is now going to pop up an external link and you can tie these together with a session

takeaways.technique: Standardized protocol between host and merchant endpoints
takeaways.what_they_do: Both OpenAI's agentic commerce protocol and Google's universal commerce protocol expose nearly identical integration points (a well-known JSON manifest plus a checkout-session endpoint), so one merchant integration serves multiple hosts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you go look at the specs, you're going to find out, oh, they are almost identical
